supports.where: Section 2, the last of the five hazard statements; the classes beside it are acute and chronic toxicity to water life, both category 1, and the sheet lists the pictogram for the environment. With it is the precautionary statement P273, that release to the environment is avoided; section 14 marks the solution a marine pollutant. The first supplier's sheet for its solution says the same of water life in words, with no class and no code. The note says that this sheet has H410 itself.

Read and not carried. Section 2, among the precautionary statements. With it are P201 and P202, on reading the instructions first; P270, that nobody eats, drinks or smokes while using the solution; P271, on good air; P280, on gloves, protective clothing and protection for the eyes and the face; P308+P313, medical attention for anyone exposed or worried; and P405 and P501, on storage and disposal. Why: the note is held to about 150 words and keeps what protects someone at the bench: it has the hood or the well-aired room from the first supplier's sheet for the solution, where a mist is drawn away.

The heading of section 4. Under it, for the eyes: contact lenses are looked for and taken out, the eyes are flushed with water for 15 minutes or more, the upper and lower lids lifted from time to time, and medical attention is got at once. The first supplier's sheet for its solution gives several minutes and no line on medical advice for the eyes; the note gives the 15 minutes and the doctor at once as what this lab goes by. The form of this supplier prints the same line for the eyes on every sheet of its that was read; it is carried all the same, as first aid on a sheet for the solution on the bench. The precautionary statements of section 2 give the rinsing of the eyes as 15 minutes too, with P305+P351+P338. Section 8 says that safety glasses, goggles or a face shield, a laboratory coat or apron and gloves are to be worn, and that an eyewash and a safety shower are to be at hand.

Section 4, the label of the first of its four lines. Under it, in capitals, that the solution may be harmful if swallowed; then that a doctor or a poison centre is called at once, and vomiting is brought on only if medical staff say so. The first supplier's sheet for its solution asks for the call if the person feels unwell, and so does this sheet's own precautionary statement P301+P330+P312. The note gives the call at once as what this lab goes by, and says nothing of vomiting. The form of this supplier prints the same line on every sheet of its that was read; it is carried all the same, because swallowing is a hazard the statements on this bottle name, and lead builds up in the body.

Section 11, after the label for signs and symptoms of exposure, the opening of its first sentence, which goes on to say that small amounts can raise what the body holds to a toxic level. The note says that lead builds up in the body.

The heading of section 6. Under it, as an environmental precaution: runoff is to be kept from storm sewers and from ditches that lead to waterways. A spill is taken up with a dry inert material and put into a container for disposal, and the place washed. Section 13 says that its guidance is for small amounts, and that disposal is to follow the local, state and federal rules or go through a licensed agency for chemical disposal; the note gives no method of disposal. The line on storm sewers is on every sheet of this supplier that was read, whatever the substance. The note carries it for lead nitrate, as keeping the solution out of drains and waterways, because this sheet classes the solution as very toxic to water life and because lead is regulated: section 14 of the sheet gives a reportable quantity of 10 lbs, and NOAA's record shows lead compounds on a list of the Environmental Protection Agency.

Read and not carried. The heading of section 12, and the last line under it: that harm to the environment cannot be ruled out if the product is handled or disposed of carelessly. Above it the section gives figures for lead nitrate with a trout and a water flea, of 2 mg/L and less. Why: the same line is on every sheet of this supplier that was read, for this lab and for the three before it, whatever the substance.
Read and not carried. Section 10, the label of its list: ammonium thiocyanate, powdered carbon and lead hypophosphite. Why: none of the three is on this bench.
